segments.title: The problem
points: Each one should be a verifiable record
segments.text: Every year, lakhs of students join AICTE-approved colleges. Each admission should be a record that is accurate, verifiable and fair to the student. But today, oversight mostly sees totals.

sentences.text: Every year, lakhs of students join AICTE-approved colleges.
Each admission should be a record that is accurate, verifiable and fair to the student.
But today, oversight mostly sees totals.

segments.title: The problem
segments.text: A college reports how many students it admitted, not who they are. Excess admissions hide inside those numbers. The same student can be enrolled at two colleges at once, and nobody notices. And when an employer asks whether a degree is real, the answer is a letter and a long wait.

sentences.text: A college reports how many students it admitted, not who they are.
Excess admissions hide inside those numbers.
The same student can be enrolled at two colleges at once, and nobody notices.
And when an employer asks whether a degree is real, the answer is a letter and a long wait.

segments.title: The idea
segments.text: The APAAR Student Register fixes this with one simple idea. Every enrolment is stored as an individual student record, keyed to the student's APAAR ID. Every number on every dashboard is computed from those records, never typed in as a total. Let's walk through every page, role by role.

sentences.text: The APAAR Student Register fixes this with one simple idea.
Every enrolment is stored as an individual student record, keyed to the student's APAAR ID.
Every number on every dashboard is computed from those records, never typed in as a total.
Let's walk through every page, role by role.

segments.title: Sign in · 7 roles
segments.text: This is the sign-in page. The prototype has seven roles: institution staff, institution admin, AICTE analyst and AICTE admin, auditor, employer or verifier, and the student. Demo accounts sign in with one click. Text size can be raised for accessibility, and every page clearly says that the data is synthetic.

sentences.text: The prototype has seven roles: institution staff, institution admin, AICTE analyst and AICTE admin, auditor, employer or verifier, and the student.
Demo accounts sign in with one click.
Text size can be raised for accessibility, and every page clearly says that the data is synthetic.

segments.title: Institution dashboard
points: Seat strip: one square per seat
segments.text: An institution starts on its dashboard. At the top are the key figures: approved intake, students within intake, seats over intake, supernumerary students, and open flags. Below, every programme has a seat strip. Each small square is one real seat: green is occupied, empty is vacant, and red would be an admission over the approved intake. Recent uploads and open flags sit on the right.

segments.title: Upload student records
segments.text: To add students in bulk, staff download the official template as Excel or CSV, fill it in, and upload it. The file is checked before anything is saved. All twenty-six validation rules run on every single row, and the summary shows how many rows are valid, need a warning, need review, or have errors.

segments.title: Fix errors row by row
points: Rule and plain explanation per error
Edit in place, leave duplicates out
segments.text: Errors are listed row by row, with the rule that failed and a plain explanation. Here, a mistyped APAAR ID gets a did-you-mean suggestion from the registry check, which is simulated in this prototype. One click accepts it. Other rows are fixed in a small editor, right inside the page. A duplicate row can simply be left out.

segments.title: Commit
points: Rows with errors are never committed
segments.text: Before committing, the register shows exactly what will happen to seat positions, programme by programme. A row with an error is never committed. Staff confirm, and the records are saved in one step. The national register updates live.

segments.title: Add a student
segments.text: Single admissions use the Add a student form. It runs the very same twenty-six rules as the upload, so there is no back door. For a student under eighteen, the form asks whether guardian consent has been recorded. Sensitive fields, like social category, are optional and clearly marked.

segments.title: Student records
points: Search by name, roll or APAAR ID
segments.text: Student records can be searched by name, roll number or APAAR ID, and sorted by any column. APAAR IDs are masked, so only the last digits show. Opening a record shows the student, the enrolment, any flags, and a full history of every change.

segments.title: Record detail
segments.text: Every correction needs a reason, which is kept in the history. Status changes, such as cancelled or graduated, follow allowed transitions only. From here, the institution also issues a signed enrolment record for the student, and can revoke it later with a reason that verifiers will see.

segments.title: Seat check
segments.text: The seat check answers one question before an admission is made: will one more student cross the approved intake or a category cap? It is advice before admission, not a penalty after. College admission software can ask the same question through the API.

segments.title: Flags
points: Evidence and rule on every flag
segments.text: When a rule finds something that needs a person to look at it, the register raises a flag. Each flag shows its evidence and its rule. The institution responds with a note, AICTE can ask for clarification, resolve or dismiss, and every step is kept in the history. A flag is a question, never an accusation.

segments.title: Correction requests
segments.text: Students can spot mistakes too. Their correction requests arrive here. Staff accept a request, which opens the correction form with the change ready, or reject it with a reason the student will see.

segments.title: Reports and system access
points: Scoped API keys for college software
segments.text: Reports download as CSV files, protected against spreadsheet formula injection. And on System access, an institution admin creates API keys with limited scopes, so its own admission software can push enrolments and run seat checks directly.

segments.title: National register (AICTE)
segments.text: Now the AICTE view. The national register shows institutions, programmes, approved intake, students within intake, utilisation and seats over intake, for the whole country, all computed from records. Excess alerts name the exact programme: Narmada's MBA has sixty-eight students against an approved intake of sixty. Below are breakdowns by state, by nationality, APAAR coverage, and open flags by rule.

segments.title: National register · tabs
segments.text: The programmes tab lists every programme with its seats, and submission status shows which colleges have declared their submission complete. Filters narrow everything by year, state and discipline, and the page updates live as institutions upload.

segments.title: Review priority
points: A reason to review, not a verdict
segments.text: Review priority helps AICTE decide where to look first. Institutions are ranked by transparent reasons, such as seats over intake, supernumerary caps, conflicts with other colleges, unverified APAAR IDs and uncorrected upload errors. The page says clearly that a high rank is a reason to review, not evidence of wrongdoing.

segments.title: Review queue
segments.text: The review queue lists every open flag across the country. AICTE can request clarification with a note, and the institution sees it immediately. Duplicates across colleges appear here too, and the other institution's identity is withheld, to protect the student.

segments.title: Intake and caps
segments.text: On Intake and caps, AICTE sets each programme's approved intake with its approval reference, and the caps for supernumerary categories. Every seat count in the system is measured against these numbers.

segments.title: Identity candidates
segments.text: Identity candidates catch the same person enrolled twice under different spellings. Name matching understands Indian spelling and transliteration variants, and every match shows its reasons and weights. A person decides: same person, or different people. Nothing is merged automatically.

segments.title: Rules and integrations
segments.text: The rules page lists all twenty-six validation rules with their codes and severity, so every flag can be traced to a published rule. The integrations page is honest about what is connected: the APAAR registry check is simulated, and DigiLocker, AISHE and the approval portal still need official access.

segments.title: Student view
segments.text: Now the student. Ananya sees her own record exactly as her college reported it. She can share a signed enrolment record, and she chooses exactly which details to include. The register creates a token and a QR code. If something is wrong, she sends a correction request to her college.

segments.title: Public verification
segments.text: An employer opens the public verify page and pastes the token. Six checks run in order: structure, a known issuer key, the signature, that the shared values match, the validity period, and revocation. All six pass, and only the details Ananya chose are shown. Now watch: change a single value, and verification fails immediately.

segments.title: Consent-based requests
points: Same answer whether or not the student exists
Student sees what will be shared
segments.text: Employers can also request verification with an APAAR ID and date of birth. The response is the same whether or not the student exists, so nobody can probe the register. The student reviews the request, sees exactly what will be shared, and allows or declines. Only after she allows does the employer see a result.

segments.title: Students under 18
segments.text: Students under eighteen are protected by rule R015. Their record cannot be shared or verified until the institution records a guardian's consent. The student sees exactly why sharing is on hold.

segments.title: Audit trail
points: Each hash covers the one before
segments.text: Every sign-in, change and access lands in a hash-chained audit trail. Each event's hash covers the one before it, so any edit to history breaks the chain. The auditor verifies the whole chain with one click, and can export it.

segments.title: System status
segments.text: Finally, a public system status page states honestly what is built and tested, what is simulated, and what still needs official access, each with the evidence behind it.

segments.title: Why it is better
segments.text: So why is this better? Seats are counted from real records, not declared totals, so excess admissions cannot hide. Duplicates across colleges are caught early, while identities stay private. Students control what they share. Employers verify in seconds instead of weeks. And every action is accountable, in a chain no one can quietly rewrite.

segments.title: Under the hood
segments.text: Under the hood, a React interface talks to a FastAPI service. One validation engine is the only writer of student records, feeding the seat ledger, identity matching and signed credentials, with every step in the audit chain, on PostgreSQL.
